concepts.title: Sources of Light and Straight-line Travel

questions.q: Name the natural source of light and two man-made sources.
questions.a: Natural: the sun. Man-made: bulb, candle, torch.

questions.q: Why do we say light travels in straight lines?
questions.a: Shadows and beams form in straight lines; light does not bend around corners on its own.

questions.q: What makes an object visible to us?
questions.a: Light from it (or reflected by it) entering our eyes.

questions.q: What are transparent, translucent and opaque objects? Give one example each.
questions.a: Transparent: glass (see through clearly). Translucent: frosted glass (blurry). Opaque: wood (no light).

questions.q: What is a shadow and when does it form?
questions.a: A dark patch where an opaque object blocks light; it forms on the side away from the light.

questions.q: Why is the shadow of a pole longest in the morning and evening?
questions.a: The sun is low then, so rays strike at a slant and shadows stretch long.

questions.q: State the law of reflection for a plane mirror.
questions.a: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.

questions.q: What image does a plane mirror form?
questions.a: An upright image of the same size as the object, laterally inverted (left-right reversed), behind the mirror.

questions.q: Why does the word 'AMBULANCE' appear mirror-written on vehicles?
questions.a: Drivers ahead see it in their mirrors; the reversal makes it read correctly in the mirror.

concepts.title: The Pinhole Camera and Useful Items

questions.q: How does a pinhole camera form an image?
questions.a: Light from each point passes through the tiny hole in straight lines, forming an inverted image on the screen.

questions.q: Why is the pinhole image upside down?
questions.a: Rays cross at the pinhole - light from the top of the object lands at the bottom of the screen.

questions.q: Name two things a pinhole camera teaches us.
questions.a: Light travels in straight lines, and images can be formed without a lens.
